chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) applies to his body and head khuluq (a type of hair oil/grease), perfume (tayyib), and a chewy substance like Roman gum (mastic) and mouth freshener, and what resembles them. He then performs ghusl (ritual bath). When he finishes, he finds something remaining on his body from the trace of the khuluq, perfume, and other things.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem (with his prayer/purity).'

key_terms.الْخَلُوقُ: A type of hair oil or grease used in antiquity
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: To be in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: Does remaining trace of hair oil or perfume invalidate ghusl for a junub person?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies that residual traces of external substances like perfume or hair oil on the body after ghusl do not invalidate ritual purity, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *istishab al-taharah* (presumption of purity) when doubt arises about minor impurities. This ruling distinguishes between the removal of the major impurity itself and the cosmetic residue, emphasizing practical ease (*rukhas*) in daily worship. It underscores the distinction between *hadath* (ritual state) and *najis* (impurity), where mere presence of non-impure residue does not break the state of purity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Mahmoud who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man comes to be with sexual impurity, so he applies his body and his head with the oil, and the perfume, and something chewy like the roman gum and the (mouth) freshener, and what resembles it, and he washes. So when he is free, he find something to have remained in his body, from the traces of the oil, and the perfume, and other’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn abu Mahmud who has said the following:

“I once asked al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Is it permissible for one after experiencing sexual relation to come in contact with perfume, oils or such things as chewing-gum or freshener, then take Ghusl (bath)? What happens if such one afterwards finds pieces left on one’s body or marks of rubbing oil or perfumes and so on?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
